content:
Earlier this month, OpenAI, together with Astra, launched its first GPT-6 model. The GPT-6 series officially debuts, adding two new variants — GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna — further expanding the product lineup.

GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna are available starting today

According to the ChatGPT desktop app's update log, GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna consume fewer tokens than their GPT-5.6 counterparts.

GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna will roll out on Codex and ChatGPT Work, with token pricing lower than the previous-generation GPT-5.6. Sol is suited for complex coding and agentic workflows, while Luna is designed for tasks requiring deep focus and high throughput. Both models will be made available in phases to Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise and Edu users. Free and Go users can access Luna via the desktop app. Actual availability will depend on the rollout schedule and workspace settings; Enterprise admins will need to enable the new models themselves. Within ChatGPT, both models are currently available only on Work and Codex, and have not yet arrived on Chat.

Worth noting: there is no such thing as GPT-6 Terra. It seems OpenAI is phasing out the mid-tier, keeping only three levels: Terra (small), Sol (large), Astra (extra large).

Below is OpenAI's official announcement:

Even though the most challenging and high-impact work still requires Astra's full depth, different tasks have different scales, rhythms and budgets. Precisely because of that, we are expanding the GPT-6 series with the launch of GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna. GPT-6 Astra ushered in a new generation of intelligence, and these two new models further improve cost efficiency, bringing those advantages to a broader range of users. We trained GPT-6 Sol and Luna using the same approach as GPT-6 Astra, distilling Astra's leading capabilities in professional work, factual accuracy, coding, computer use and model alignment into faster, more economical models.

The company said both new models outperform GPT-5.6 and are priced lower than Astra (as well as the GPT-5.6 version it replaced). For example, the GPT-6 versions of Sol and Luna are priced 50% lower than their GPT-5.6 counterparts.
